attacks.claim: Dark mode is broken for day cards. `.day-card` hardcodes a white background while its text uses `var(--text)`, which becomes near-white (#f2f2f7) under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`. For the ~30% of users on dark OS settings, card titles and meta text would be near-invisible on white. The QA covers only light mode, so this is untested.
attacks.evidence: .day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... } vs --text: #f2f2f7 under prefers-color-scheme: dark; QA: "Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass"

attacks.claim: The 72px fixed mobile action bar has no bottom padding on `.planner` or `body` and no safe-area inset. The last day (Sunday) and its tiles can be hidden behind the bar at 360–414px, and the bar can overlap the iOS home indicator.
attacks.evidence: .action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... } with "Sunday is the last child of .planner"; .planner { ... padding: 16px; ... }

attacks.claim: The most frequent action (about 9.4 shopping-list adds per user per week, 64% on mobile) goes from a one-tap "+ List" button to a multi-step flow through the recipe page, Ingredients tab, and servings sheet. The brief does not show that users want decluttered tiles more than this one-tap add, and the artifact has no metric or test for task cost. The watch list tracks aggregate adds/WAU with no per-step funnel for this path.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level \"+ List\" button is removed to declutter tiles." / "tap the tile → recipe page → \"Ingredients\" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → \"Add to list\" → toast with \"Undo\"" / "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: "Share plan" exposes the user's meal and schedule data outward, but the artifact does not specify the share mechanism: link scope, token unguessability, expiry, revocation, or data included. It also has no consent, disclosure, or retention statement for shared plans or for the new telemetry events.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Share plan</button> — ABSENT: share scope, link generation, token handling, expiry, access control, or consent/retention statement

attacks.claim: QA does not cover the viewports and input modes that carry most of the traffic: 360px-wide Android, touch drag-and-drop, or dark mode. The release goes to 100% of web users at once, so untested mobile and dark-mode defects would reach everyone.
attacks.evidence: "Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass"; "Drag-and-drop between days ... pass" (no device or input detail); "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT"

attacks.claim: The rollout goes from zero to 100% of web users in one step even though a `planner_v7` flag exists. There is no staged percentage or canary, so a regression such as the dark-mode or action-bar defect would reach every user before anyone can measure it.

"Generate shopping list" adds all planned recipes for the week with no stated behavior for duplicates, existing list items, confirmation, or undo. A single tap can silently change the existing list. Because the rollback is flag-only with no data migration, shopping-list writes made through this action would persist after the flag is flipped off.
attacks.evidence: "Generate shopping list" (adds all planned recipes for the week) / "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)"

attacks.claim: Each tile's "Swap" button has no recipe-specific accessible name, so screen-reader users hear up to 21 identical "Swap" controls. Only the overflow button is labeled with the recipe name.
attacks.evidence: <button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button> vs <button class="btn-icon" aria-label="More options for Sheet-pan gnocchi">⋯</button>

attacks.claim: Drag-to-move is specified with no touch-gesture design for mobile, which is 68% of sessions. Touch drag can conflict with page scrolling, and the artifact does not address this.
attacks.evidence: "Drag a recipe tile between days to move it." — ABSENT: touch drag behavior on mobile

attacks.claim: The tile image is a single 320px asset with no srcset or sizes, and the only performance evidence is one Lighthouse mobile run (performance 91, CLS 0.01). The image weight across 360–414px viewports and the aspect-ratio match across breakpoints are not shown.
attacks.evidence: / "Lighthouse mobile: performance 91, accessibility 100, CLS 0.01"

attacks.claim: The flag rollback only restores the old planner if the old markup and CSS still ship alongside the new ones. The artifact asserts this but does not confirm that the old code path is retained.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)." — ABSENT: confirmation that old planner markup/CSS is retained
